subject: Post-call: Reserved GPU needs, isolation and SLOs for Cerebra Labs
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cerebralabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: reserved capacity, isolation, SLOs

Hi Sanjay — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our side and next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Key pain points you shared
- Production latency spikes for peak inference (95th pctl frequently > 300ms) impacting inference-heavy features.
- Regulatory requirement to logically isolate PHI workloads and control egress (want private VPC + KMS).
- Unpredictable monthly costs when using on-demand or shared pools.

2) Goals you outlined
- Target 95th percentile token latency < 150ms for standard NLU endpoints.
- Reserve the equivalent of ~20 A100-class GPUs (initial) with burst capacity for model fine-tuning/evals.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for inference endpoints; audit logs retained for 12 months.

3) What Redwood can deliver (high level)
- Dedicated reserved GPU pool with tenant isolation (VPC peering + optional on-prem connector).
- Autoscaling and burst policies to handle evaluation windows without impacting baseline SLOs.
- Token-level cost reporting and ops runbook for fallbacks.

4) Agreed next steps (owner / ETA)
- You: share a short workload profile (qps distribution, typical seq lengths, batch sizes) — Sanjay / by Fri 6/13.
- Us: draft a Mutual Action Plan and an initial PO/pricing sketch — Rishi / by Thu 6/12.
- Tech deep-dive (1hr) with infra + security to review VPC/KMS options — schedule for week of 6/16.

Attachments: I asked for a simple infrastructure worksheet you can populate — send back when convenient (stub: infrastructure_requirements.xlsx).

If any bullets above don't match your memory, tell me and I'll update. Otherwise I'll circulate the MAP and draft pricing tomorrow and we can lock a time for the technical session.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0123

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cerebralabs.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 18:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: reserved capacity, isolation, SLOs

Rishi — thanks, this is great and accurate. A few clarifications and I attached the worksheet you mentioned.

Clarifications:
- The 95th pctl target of <150ms is for our customer-facing NLU endpoints (avg seq len ~120 tokens). Internal batch jobs can tolerate higher latency.
- For reserved capacity, we expect an initial baseline of 12 GPUs but need burst up to ~28 GPUs during model evaluation windows (every ~6 weeks).
- Compliance: SOC2 in progress; we need help documenting audit log retention and KMS key lifecycle for the sales/infosec review.

Attached: infrastructure_requirements.xlsx (stub with QPS, seq length, and current traffic spikes).

Appreciate the MAP and pricing. For scheduling: Thurs 6/19 or Mon 6/23 are good for our infra folks.

—Sanjay

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cerebralabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: reserved capacity, isolation, SLOs — MAP + SLO draft

Sanjay — appreciate the worksheet, got it and reviewed. I've drafted a short Mutual Action Plan and an SLO summary (attached: redwood_mutual_action_plan.pdf). Highlights below: 

SLO summary (proposed)
- Availability: 99.9% platform uptime for reserved pool endpoints (excludes planned maintenance windows with 7-day notice).
- Latency: 95th percentile token-serving latency goal <150ms for production NLU endpoints under baseline load; burst windows will have documented degradation modes and fallback to lower-cost variants.
- Auditability: Request/response logs and token-level usage retained for 12 months; access via console + KMS-managed keys.

Proposed capacity plan
- Baseline: 12 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool (isolated tenant).
- Burst policy: Allow burst up to additional 16 GPUs for 48–72 hour evaluation windows; bursts are metered and billed at pre-agreed rates.
- Autoscale behavior: Prefetch and continuous batching enabled; option to pin models to pool for guaranteed cache heat.

Next actions (owners updated)
- Sanjay: confirm the baseline vs burst numbers in the worksheet and sign off on SLOs / by Tue 6/16.
- Rishi: share preliminary pricing (workbook) and contract routing (legal/compliance contacts) — by Thu 6/12 (attached pricing_draft_v1.xlsx).
- Marissa: lead procurement cadence and prepare standard reserved capacity offer (Marissa / by Fri 6/13).

If that alignment looks right I'll schedule the 1hr technical session with our infra + security team (I propose Tue 6/17 at 10am PT).

Best,
Rishi

Attachments: redwood_mutual_action_plan.pdf, pricing_draft_v1.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotha <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: reserved capacity, isolation, SLOs — internal pricing note

Rishi — quick internal note. I updated pricing_draft_v1.xlsx with a tiered reserved-rate and burst surcharge. Key points for negotiation:
- Offer a 10% pre-pay discount on the first 6-month commit to reduce Cerebra's cost variability.
- Include a 30-day service credit SLAs clause for sustained downtime beyond the 99.9% target.
- Flag legal: need a short data processing addendum for KMS/PHI handling.

I'll stand by to join the tech session and own the procurement thread. Please push the MAP to Sanjay and schedule the 6/17 10am PT slot if that works for their team.
